title: Log analysis: spotting an incident
summary: Read a day of web and SSH logs with grep, awk and sort. Find the scanner, find the break-in, and block it.

nodes.webserver: a web server whose logs you are investigating

tasks.title: How busy was the day?
tasks.text: How many requests are recorded in `/var/log/nginx/access.log`?
hints: Each request is one line. `wc -l` counts lines.

tasks.title: Who got the most 404s?
tasks.text: A burst of `404 Not Found` responses from one address usually means someone is guessing paths. Which IP address received the most 404s?
hints: Field 9 of each line is the status code and field 1 the client IP. `awk '$9 == 404 {print $1}'` prints the IP of every 404.
Count per IP with `sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head`.

answer_cmd.cmd: awk '$9 == 404 {print $1}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1 | awk '{print $2}'

tasks.title: Did the probing find anything?
tasks.text: Of the paths that address requested, one returned **200 OK**. Which path?
hints: Filter for that IP and status 200: `grep <ip> access.log | awk '$9 == 200 {print $7}'`.

tasks.title: The password guesser
tasks.text: Now `/var/log/auth.log`. One address failed SSH logins dozens of times. Which address?
hints: `grep 'Failed password' /var/log/auth.log` shows failures. The IP follows the word `from`.

answer_cmd.cmd: grep 'Failed password' /var/log/auth.log | grep -o 'from [0-9.]*' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1 | awk '{print $3}'

tasks.title: Did it work?
tasks.text: After all those failures, that address **logged in successfully**. As which user account? (This is the moment an incident starts.)
hints: Look for `Accepted` lines from that address: `grep Accepted /var/log/auth.log | grep <ip>`.

answer_cmd.cmd: grep 'Accepted' /var/log/auth.log | grep {{GUESSER}} | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="for") print $(i+1)}' | head -1

tasks.title: Contain it
tasks.text: First containment step: on **webserver**, add a firewall rule that drops all incoming traffic from the address that broke in.

checks.cmd: iptables -C INPUT -s {{GUESSER}} -j DROP 2>/dev/null || iptables -C INPUT -s {{GUESSER}}/32 -j DROP
checks.fail_msg: No INPUT rule dropping that address yet.

hints: Lab 7 used the FORWARD chain. Traffic to this machine itself goes through `INPUT`: `iptables -A INPUT -s <ip> -j DROP`.

solution.note: Blocking the address is only the first step. In a real incident you would also disable or reset the account, kill its sessions, check what it did (`last`, shell history, new files), and find out why a guessable password was allowed over SSH at all.
